C. HYDROLOGY AND WATER QUALITY
Many of the residential structures to receive loans and grants for rehabilitation are within the area subject to potential inundation. Flood insurance work currently in progress to determine the exact boundaries of the flood plains will refine the inundation information. Any new structures built in flood areas should include flood-proofing in the design. The Alma Neighborhood Center, the Alum Rock Senior Center, and the Olinder Library are all in areas presently defined as subject to flooding. Flood insurance, as required by Federal law, will be required for those structures determined to be within the one percent flood zone.
The proposed storm drain inprovements in the Alviso and Gardner neighborhoods will have a positive impact upon the localized flooding conditions.
Water quality in the San Jose area will be positively affected by the CDBG program proposals to improve sanitary sewer facilities and streets in some neighborhoods. Improvement to old and damaged sanitary sewer lines will reduce the amount of sewerage leakage thereby improving the quality of groundwater resources.
Street and sewer improvements which involve disturbing the ground surface, may cause minor and temporary siltation which will have a short lived adverse impact on water quality. Site preparations for the Alma Neighborhood Center and the Alum Rock Senior Center will involve impacts of the same degree and transitory nature. These are extremely minor impacts.
D. FLORA AND FAUNA
None of the projects in the three year CDBG will affect any rare or endangered species. This project will not have any significant impact upon our animal life and with perhaps two possible exceptions described below, no vegetation will be adversely affected.
Alma CNRA:
The Alma Neighborhood Center is the only project which could impact trees, and this structure will be sited to preserve specimen trees.
Alviso CNRA:
The storm lines construction in Alviso and street improvements will not impact any street trees or other significant vegetation.
Campus CNRA:
Trees and other vegetation in the Campus area will not be impacted by either the loans and grants program, or rehabilitation to John XXIII Senior Center.
